title: Fast Computation of Kemeny’s Constant for Directed Graphs

problem.claim: Estimating Kemeny’s constant for large directed graphs is computationally challenging.

gap.claim: Existing approximation methods are limited by reliance on undirected-graph properties or inefficient simulation.

contributions.claim: Two approximation algorithms for estimating Kemeny’s constant on directed graphs.
The proposed algorithms provide theoretical error guarantees.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the two approximation algorithms as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive numerical experiments on real-world networks report that the algorithms outperform baseline methods in efficiency and accuracy.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines Kemeny’s constant through stationary-distribution-weighted mean hitting time.
Notes broad applications and research interest.
Identifies poor scaling of exact matrix-inversion computation and limitations of existing approximations.
Introduces two directed-graph approximation algorithms with theoretical error guarantees.
Reports numerical validation on real-world networks against baseline methods.

source_observation.claim: Approximation methods are motivated by the poor scaling of exact computation on large networks.

interpretation.claim: When exact computation does not scale, approximation can target practical efficiency while retaining explicit error control.

application.claim: For large directed-network metrics, pair scalable approximation with theoretical error guarantees.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish performance across all graph classes or network sizes.

unknowns: Algorithmic details and computational complexity are not provided.
The form of the theoretical error guarantees is not specified.
The evaluated networks, baselines, and quantitative results are not identified.
